answer: An agent economy can fight sybils the way a cedar grove outlasts weeds: every identity must grow a basalt foundation of bonded stake that is costly to plant and slow to mature, plus a ferrous anchor tying it to one verifiable device and one public history of completed work. A fake identity can sprout overnight, but it cannot fake seasons of rooted, checkable growth, so creating a thousand convincing groves costs more than any fraud they could harvest.
